artifacts.summary: Traces test-mcp-merge-target.sh Assertions C/E to merge.lua's remove_tracked 'new_object' wholesale-removal bug; confirms the fix already landed via commit 3c7f91a92 before this dispatch, the suite now passes 7/0 deterministically on two direct runs, and no further code change is needed -- remaining work is confirmatory (full verify-deploy.sh + deploy-headless.sh, deferred here to the batch's own gate stage).

memory_candidates.content: merge.lua's remove_tracked() (extension merge-target unmerge path) treated 'new_array'/'new_object'/'new_value' tracked-entry types identically (unconditional wholesale t[key]=nil). This is correct for a scalar or freshly-created array but wrong for 'new_object': deep_merge's 'Object: recurse' arm always tracks a new object's children individually, so wholesale removal destroys any sibling key added into that same object after the extension's own first load (e.g. a hand-written .mcp.json mcpServers entry surviving a forced-reload regenerate). Fixed by giving 'new_object' its own branch that recurses into tracked children (mirroring the 'merged' branch) and only prunes the object once empty. Generalizes: any object-keyed (not array-keyed) merge target in this engine was exposed to this class of defect until the object-vs-scalar/array distinction was made explicit in remove_tracked.

An unfiltered verify-deploy.sh invocation refuses with a 'DEFERRED: a batch-gate-pending marker exists' message when the current /orchestrate batch cycle already owes the full gate set to its own once-per-invocation batch-gate stage. --override-batch-gate-deferral is reserved for that stage's own discharger; a concurrent dispatch (e.g. a research/plan dispatch running alongside sibling implement dispatches in the same cycle) should use --only-gate/--gate8-touched for a scoped check instead of forcing the override.
